question: Should these approval-auth and secret-target builders become supported public Plugin SDK contracts once representative live parity proof is supplied?
rationale: The helpers are additive and appear mechanically sound, but they centralize authorization and credential metadata across many channels; tests alone cannot establish that maintainers intend to support this exact public abstraction and policy boundary.

options.title: Approve After Parity Proof
options.body: Accept the public helpers after representative live authorization and secret-management evidence confirms channel behavior is unchanged.

options.title: Narrow The Public Surface
options.body: Keep the internal deduplication but expose fewer helpers or lower-level primitives until the long-term external plugin contract is clearer.

options.title: Retain Local Security Contracts
options.body: Merge only the config-hint and directory helpers while leaving approval and secret contracts channel-owned.

recommendation.title: Approve After Parity Proof
recommendation.body: Accept the public helpers after representative live authorization and secret-management evidence confirms channel behavior is unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged feature-history precedent is the shared native approval route-gate work, which addressed the same generic-versus-channel-owned authorization boundary.
